clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-month-old female with history of prematurity and prolonged neonatal intubation (1 month) presented with progressive biphasic stridor and respiratory distress misdiagnosed as recurrent croup on multiple prior admissions. She acutely decompensated following fever and diarrhea. Physical examination revealed irritability, tachypnea, tachycardia, biphasic stridor with suprasternal/intercostal retractions, and weak cry unrelieved by positional changes. Pre-operative workup included a negative COVID-19 test and lateral neck radiograph demonstrating significant subglottic airway compromise (figure 1A). With a presumptive diagnosis of subglottic cyst, she underwent emergency tracheotomy with mask ventilation. Direct laryngoscopy revealed a submucosal cystic lesion immediately beneath the mobile vocal cords without significant patent airway around the cyst (figure 2A). Intraoperative management included aspiration of 1 mL thick yellowish clear fluid via 22-gauge microlaryngeal needle and marsupialization of the right posterolateral subglottic cyst using coblator. Postoperatively, she recovered well, was discharged with a corked tracheostomy tube and nasal breathing. Follow-up endoscopic evaluation at 2 months showed no cyst recurrence, with delayed decannulation planned due to the COVID-19 pandemic/lockdown.

Direct laryngoscopy revealed cystic lesion rather than circumferential stenosis, though this was in the differential given intubation history
